title: 1976 AHSME Problem 21

concepts.label: Sum of first n odd numbers

statement: What is the smallest positive odd integer \(n\) such that the product \[ 2^{\frac{1}{7}}2^{\frac{3}{7}}\cdots2^{\frac{2n+1}{7}} \] is greater than \(1000?\) (In the product the denominators of the exponents are all sevens, and the numerators are the successive odd integers from \(1\) to \(2n+1.\))

solutions.text:
The product is \[ 2^{\frac{1+3+\cdots+(2n+1)}{7}} =2^{\frac{(n+1)^2}{7}}. \] For \(n=7,\) the exponent \(\frac{64}{7}\) is less than \(\frac{19}{2},\) so the product is less than \(2^{\frac{19}{2}}=512\sqrt2\lt768\lt1000.\) All smaller positive odd \(n\) also fail. For \(n=9,\) the exponent is \(\frac{100}{7}\gt10,\) so the product exceeds \(2^{10}=1024.\) Thus the first allowable odd \(n\) is \(9.\)

Therefore, the correct answer is B.
hints: Combine the powers by summing the odd numerators
The odd-number sum \(1+3+\cdots+(2n+1)\) equals \((n+1)^2;\) compare with \(2^{10}=1024\)
